eyebrow: Python for Data Engineers · Chapter 4, Lesson 19
subtitle: Meet the two structures the rest of this chapter is built on.

code:
import pandas as pd

prices = pd.Series([129.99, 249.50, 79.00, 45.25], name="unit_price")
print(prices)

# 0    129.99
# 1    249.50
# 2     79.00
# 3     45.25
# Name: unit_price, dtype: float64
caption: Every value has a label — the index — not just a position. A list has no equivalent concept.

code:
sample = pd.DataFrame({
    "order_id": [1001, 1002, 1003],
    "product": ["Trail Runner GTX", "Alpine 2P Tent", "Summit Daypack 22L"],
    "quantity": [2, 1, 1],
    "unit_price": [129.99, 249.50, 79.00],
})
print(sample)
caption: A 2-D table where each column is its own Series, all sharing one row index.

eyebrow: A first real look at orders.csv
code:
df = pd.read_csv("orders.csv")

print(df.shape)
print(df.dtypes)

# (20, 10)
# quantity         int64
# unit_price     float64
# order_date      object
# ...
caption: df.shape is (rows, columns). Pandas infers type, not correctness — it won't flag order 1014's quantity of -1.
